items.title: Dick Spottswood interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, February 13, 2023
items.q: There’s a wonderful photo in a Bob Wills book of Bob and Henry Allen and Tommy Duncan and one or two other jazz people... Those musicians knew each other.

ctx.x: They danced like people did in the southwest, you know like those wonderful Bennie Moten records throughout the twenties and early thirties. Like those few location recordings that were made by the Basie band right after it came out of Kansas City into Chicago and to New York. And some of those other territory bands, I can’t think of names right off the hand, but when you could hear other music from the southwest you’re hearing Charlie Christian, you’re hearing Bob Wills, you’re hearing Milton Brown, you’re…

somebody, all sitting around the table having drinks together in the forties. Those musicians knew each other. They didn’t have those problems. The music was the music and if you heard a Bob Wills record without singing you wouldn’t think it was a white band. Their version of “White Heat” really skunks the Jimmie Lunceford version.
